title: High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy Revealed Dynamic Polymerization of MamK Cytoskeleton for Magnetosome Positioning
content: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) have magnetic organelles, termed magnetosomes, which consist of a magnetic particle enveloped by lipid membranes. MTB utilizes magnetosomes to sense the geomagnetic field and swim along the geomagnetic field (magnetotaxis). Combinative use of magnetotaxis and aerotaxis helps MTB effectively seek microaerobic environments that are optimal areas for growth. Magnetosomes are positioned in a chain-like configuration, acting as an effective magnetic sensor. However, the positioning mechanism of bacteria organelles has been poorly characterized. MamK, an actin-like protein, was the first protein identified to be involved in magnetosome positioning, forming helical double-stranded cytoskeletal filaments that bind to magnetosomes [1, 2]. In 2017, Taoka et al. reported that the MamK cytoskeleton protects magnetosome chains from physical disturbances such as aggregation and dispersion, and immobilizes them into a static chain-like configuration [3]. Another essential protein is MamJ. MamJ is conserved in the genomes of the genus Magnetospirillum. MamJ was thought necessary for proper MamK structure and its dynamics [4]. These results suggested that MamJ acts as a factor that regulates the MamK cytoskeleton. However, the molecular roles of MamJ remain unclear.
